solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Pop round with ring, or call? (6)

indicators.note: to turn something round is to face it the other way

blocks.note: pop = PA, a father, turned round
a peal is a ring of bells

annotation.surface: Someone dropping in on a neighbour, wondering whether to ring the doorbell or give them a call.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Pop round' reads as a casual visit; it is dad written backwards. 'With' only glues the pieces.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the sense of a plea: a public appeal for witnesses is a call for them.

entries.clue: Cutting from cedar bore a leaf like this? (8)

annotation.definition: Cutting from cedar bore a leaf like this?

indicators.note: a cutting is a slip taken out of a longer stem, so the answer is a slice from the words that follow

annotation.surface: A gardener taking a cutting from a cedar and finding it has put out a leaf.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both instruction and definition: a leaf growing on a cedar cutting is, fittingly, tree-like.
annotation.definitionFit: Read straight, the clue describes a leaf from a tree, and arboreal is the adjective for anything belonging to trees.

entries.clue: It’s a reservation, or so VIP arranged (7)

indicators.note: to arrange letters is to put them in a new order

annotation.surface: A restaurant table booked, or so the maître d' says, by some very important person.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Reservation' looks like a restaurant booking; here it is a condition or qualification attached to an agreement.
annotation.definitionFit: Reservation in its contractual sense, a limiting condition, which is exactly what a proviso written into an agreement is.

entries.clue: Drink occasionally calms earl, if cha in pot (9)

indicators.note: only now and then, so only every other letter counts

blocks.clueFragment: calms earl, if cha in pot
blocks.note: the even letters: cAlMs EaRl If ChA iN pOt

annotation.surface: An earl soothed by having tea in the pot now and then.
annotation.walkthrough: The tea surface points to cha; the drink is a coffee, espresso topped up with hot water.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by category: the americano is one kind of coffee drink.

entries.clue: Fool covering over head, overcome meeting king (8)

annotation.surface: A court jester in a hood besting the king he is brought before.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Fool' reads as the jester noun; it is the verb, to trick.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym for the verb: both mean to deceive, hoodwink originally being to blindfold someone with a hood.

entries.clue: Murderous milieu of “Mr Ice”? (9,5)

blocks.note: read cryptically, MR ICE is what you get when CRIME is organised into a new order

annotation.surface: A gangland figure known as Mr Ice and the violent world he moves in.
annotation.walkthrough: Read the answer as an instruction and it produces the nickname; the mob nickname in turn makes the gangster world the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Organised crime is the violent world of gangsters, the natural home of someone called Mr Ice.

entries.clue: Fading colouring lacks energy (5)

indicators.note: something that lacks a thing is without it, so the letter is missing from the word

annotation.surface: A dyed fabric losing its vividness.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads as colour losing strength; the answer is a word for fading.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a dying light or sound is one fading away.

entries.clue: This person will head for disorder (7)

blocks.note: I'll = I will, the setter speaking

annotation.surface: Someone announcing they will set off towards chaos.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Head' looks like a verb of motion; it is a noun, a headland, as in Orford Ness on the Suffolk coast.
annotation.definitionFit: Disorder in its medical sense, as in a digestive disorder, is a plain synonym for an illness.

entries.clue: Initially yarn’s twisted trying out needle-less knitting – flipping puzzling! (6)

indicators.note: at the start, so take the opening letter of each word
flipping something turns it back to front

blocks.clueFragment: yarn’s twisted trying out needle-less knitting
blocks.note: Yarn's Twisted Trying Out Needle-less Knitting

annotation.surface: A knitter trying to work without needles and ending up with tangled yarn, cursing it as flipping puzzling.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Flipping' reads as a mild British swear word; it is the instruction to turn the letters round.
annotation.definitionFit: Knotty in its figurative sense: a knotty problem is tangled and hard to solve, just as the yarn is.

entries.clue: These newly spliced girls, wed, haunt Ma if short of capital? (9-2-3)

annotation.definition: These newly spliced girls, wed, haunt Ma if short of capital?

indicators.note: spliced means joined in a new arrangement, so the letters are rearranged
missing its capital letter, so MA drops its M

annotation.surface: Newly married young women who pester their mother-in-law for money.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition too: freshly married girls who visit their husband's mother when short of cash. 'Spliced' is British slang for married.
annotation.definitionFit: Read straight, the clue pictures newly married girls visiting the husband's mother for money, and that is what daughters-in-law are to her.

entries.clue: Septuagenarian maybe called up to avoid second Republican bounce back (9)

indicators.note: to avoid something is to keep clear of it, so that letter is kept out of the result

blocks.note: a baby boomer, born after the Second World War, now in their seventies
rang = called up on the phone
R = Republican; the second of the two Rs goes

annotation.surface: A politician in his seventies phoning round to escape a Republican challenger and make a comeback.
annotation.walkthrough: Joining the two pieces puts two Rs side by side; 'second Republican' tells you which one to drop.
annotation.definitionFit: Boomerang as a verb, named after the thrown stick that returns: a plan that boomerangs bounces back on its maker.

entries.clue: House I found with grand throne room (5)

blocks.note: the throne is jokey slang for the toilet, so the throne room is the loo

annotation.surface: A stately house with a grand throne room.
annotation.walkthrough: The throne room reads as royal; it is the toilet, 'loo' being everyday British for it.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: an igloo is one kind of house, built of snow blocks.

entries.clue: Coming down or stepping up, changing direction halfway (7)

indicators.note: the middle letter is a compass point, and changing direction swaps it for another

annotation.surface: Someone either stepping down or stepping up, and turning around halfway through.
annotation.walkthrough: S and N are both compass directions, so swapping the middle letter is literally changing direction.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: when rain is coming down, it is raining, as in 'it's coming down in buckets'.

entries.clue: Ignore indoctrination, e.g., lecturer has jammed in (7)

indicators.note: the answer is wedged inside the words before it

annotation.surface: Advice to disregard a lecturer who has been cramming propaganda into students.
annotation.walkthrough: The punctuation of 'e.g.' breaks the letters up to hide them.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym for the verb: to neglect a duty is to ignore it.

entries.clue: Savour a city with Italian styling … (5)

blocks.note: Rome as the Italians spell it

annotation.surface: Tasting a city done up in Italian style, leading into the next clue.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Savour' is the noun, a smell or flavour, not the verb to relish. The ellipsis joins it to the next clue for the surface only.
annotation.definitionFit: Savour as a noun is a characteristic smell or taste, a plain synonym for aroma.

entries.clue: … try consuming Italian wine, most delicious (8)

indicators.note: eating something takes it inside

blocks.note: Asti, the sparkling wine of Piedmont

annotation.surface: Continuing the Italian tour by sampling the finest local wine.
annotation.walkthrough: The ellipsis carries on from 14 across, so the Italian theme runs through both surfaces.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the superlative of tasty, matching the superlative 'most delicious'.

entries.clue: So Anna makes naan (6,3)

blocks.note: read straight, a cook at work; read cryptically, a way of transforming the name
move the middle NN of ANNA to the outside and the As to the inside

annotation.surface: A cook named Anna baking flatbread.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface invites a picture of cooking; the letters of the name are what get turned round, middle to edges.
annotation.definitionFit: Turning ANNA inside out produces NAAN, so the phrase names how one becomes the other.

entries.clue: To be honest, sweet includes fritter with the end cut off (8)

indicators.note: to include is to hold inside
the last letter is removed

blocks.clueFragment: fritter with the end cut off
blocks.note: to idle away time is to fritter it; IDLE loses its end

annotation.surface: A frank confession that a dessert contains a fried fritter, minus its tip.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Fritter' is the verb, to waste time, not the fried batter the sweet surface suggests.
annotation.definitionFit: An adverb matched by an adverbial phrase: 'to be honest' and 'candidly' both open a frank remark.

entries.clue: Eccentric hoarder stashing book away couldn’t stand (8)

indicators.note: odd, off-centre, so the letters are jumbled
to stash something is to hide it inside
stashed away, tucked in out of sight

annotation.surface: An odd hoarder hiding a book he couldn't bear to look at.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Book' goes in right after the first letter of the rearranged word; 'away' only finishes the phrase 'stashing away'.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the past tense: to abhor is to find something unbearable.

entries.clue: Bedroom in Brazilian city – couple bowled over (7)

indicators.note: turned over, so the letters come back to front

blocks.note: b = bowled on a cricket scorecard

annotation.surface: A couple knocked flat by a bedroom they find in Rio.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bowled over' reads as astonished; it splits into the cricket scorecard abbreviation for bowled and 'over' to turn the lot round.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym with a period flavour: a boudoir is a lady's private bedroom or dressing room.

entries.clue: Music from South America echoed around Lima (5)

indicators.note: an echo repeats, so SA appears twice
the pair sits on either side of what follows

blocks.note: L = Lima in the NATO phonetic alphabet

annotation.surface: Latin American music resounding round the Peruvian capital.
annotation.walkthrough: Lima looks like the city, which suits the surface; it is the radio code word for L.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by category: salsa is one style of Latin American dance music.

entries.clue: Academic, 50, got paid (7)

annotation.surface: A fifty-year-old lecturer who has drawn a salary.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Academic' reads as a noun, a lecturer; it is the adjective, scholarly.
annotation.definitionFit: Both adjectives describe someone of deep scholarship, as in a learned journal or an academic one.

entries.clue: Second time in Paris, and carrying on in road (6)

indicators.note: to carry is to hold within

annotation.surface: A second stay in Paris, carrying on down the road.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Carrying on' looks like one phrase meaning continuing, but it splits: 'carrying' holds, and 'on' is the thing held.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, though strictly a street is a road lined with buildings.

entries.clue: Turning 22 shortly, a friend in France – wave from afar? (7)

indicators.note: turning something round puts it back to front
in short form, so the abbreviation

annotation.surface: A French friend waving from a distance.
annotation.walkthrough: The wave is a sea wave, and 'from afar' hints at the word coming from Japanese as well as the wave travelling across an ocean.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition with a question mark: a tsunami is a sea wave often born far away, and a loanword from distant Japan.

entries.clue: Daughter holds up end of prayer finding change (5)

indicators.note: in a down answer, the letter underneath supports what sits above it

blocks.note: the word that ends a prayer

annotation.surface: A daughter delaying the close of grace and so altering the routine.
annotation.walkthrough: 'End of prayer' wants to be a last letter, R; it is the whole word that closes a prayer.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym for the verb, as when a bill or a text is amended, i.e. changed.

entries.clue: Award given for foul seaside resort by Democrat (3,4)

blocks.note: Redcar, a seaside town in North Yorkshire

annotation.surface: A prize handed out for a nasty seaside town next to a Democrat.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Foul' reads as an adjective for the resort; it is the football noun. 'Award' is cheeky: a red card is given against a player.
annotation.definitionFit: An ironic definition: the referee 'awards' a red card, sending a footballer off for a serious foul.

entries.clue: Kindle fine to charge night before (5)

indicators.note: charging something fills it, so the letters go inside

blocks.note: the eve is the night before

annotation.surface: A fine imposed the night before an event.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Kindle' reads as the e-reader, or as lighting a fire; it is the verb to stir up a feeling.
annotation.definitionFit: Kindle in its figurative sense, to arouse a memory or emotion, which is what evoke means.

entries.clue: US city politician I saved in overdose took off (9)

indicators.note: something saved is kept safe inside

blocks.note: I is the Roman numeral one

annotation.surface: An American politician in a city rescued after an overdose.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Took off' reads as departed; it means mimicked, as a comic takes off a politician.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: to take someone off is to mock them by imitation, which is to lampoon them.

entries.clue: Grow sad, decline (4,4)

blocks.note: to turn = to grow or become, as in turn nasty

annotation.surface: Becoming gloomy and going downhill.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Decline' sits next to 'sad' as if it meant fade; it is the verb, to refuse.
annotation.definitionFit: A phrasal verb matched to a plain one: to turn down an invitation and to decline it are the same refusal.

entries.clue: Laboured to get new dog in pig’s place (6)

indicators.note: made new, so the letters are rearranged
the new dog goes in the pig's place, so inside the sty

blocks.note: a sty is where a pig lives

annotation.surface: A farmer struggling to put a new dog where the pig used to live.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Laboured' is the adjective, heavy and dull, as in laboured prose, not the past tense of work.
annotation.definitionFit: Applied to writing, both words mean heavy and effortful: stodgy prose is laboured prose.
